summary: New York's governor and NYSERDA award about $228 million to five port and maritime projects (including the Ports of Coeymans and Albany) from offshore wind supply-chain grant money that the state redirected to broader maritime infrastructure; NYSERDA says the state still intends to pursue offshore wind in the mid and longer term.

The Senate passes H.R. 2347, the vehicle for the bipartisan permitting bill (BAAJA), 62-33 (roll call vote no. 270); the bill includes provisions giving legal recourse when an administration revisits permits or disfavors particular energy sources, which supporters say would protect permitted wind and solar projects.
next: House consideration after the Thanksgiving recess

summary: The Senate adopted the Capito substitute amendment 69-27 and then invoked cloture 65-31 on H.R. 2347, the legislative vehicle for the bipartisan permitting bill, clearing the last procedural step before a final passage vote. Some outlets reported the 65-31 vote as final passage, but the Senate roll call lists it as a cloture vote and Bloomberg Law reports passage is still to come.
source: U.S. Senate roll call votes (Nos. 267 and 268)

summary: The Army Corps of Engineers says it is reevaluating its approval of Atlantic Shores South (up to 200 turbines about 9 miles off Atlantic City); it gave no reasons or timeline. This follows the March EPA air permit invalidation and the August remand of BOEM's plan approval.

The Senate votes 70-27 to end debate on the revised bipartisan permitting bill (BAAJA), which covers wind; the President has repeated that he will not approve wind turbines regardless. The source says the vote was 'last night' relative to its Nov 17 publication.

The court grants the wind groups' request for more time to reply in support of their motion to enforce the injunction against DoD's wind-review freeze, moving their deadline to Dec. 17 so they can review DoD's next status report; the groups also tell the court DoD has countersigned mitigation agreements for some projects (Renewable Northwest v. Hegseth, D. Or.).
mission: Clearinghouse review process
next: Plaintiffs' reply due 2026-12-17; DoD response due 2026-12-24

summary: Ocean City council votes 7-0 to oppose offshore wind outright, not only turbines close to shore.
President Trump says he will not approve wind turbines, as the Senate votes 73-25 to take up a bipartisan permitting bill that covers wind.
next: Senate passed the bill 2026-11-19; House consideration after the Thanksgiving recess

summary: Revolution Wind (704 MW) reaches full operation.

A DoD declaration filed in the Oregon case (by Dale Marks) says about 400 wind projects are queued for review and eight civilian officials can sign off on them; about 33 projects have signed mitigation agreements, about 110 are in talks, and 52 were screened as causing no interference, most of them after more than 75 days.
mission: Clearinghouse review process
next: Plaintiffs' reply due 2026-12-17; DoD response due 2026-12-24

summary: Vineyard Wind 1 reaches full commercial operation.
Court filings show DoD has replaced its standard mitigation agreement of about 20 pages with a 119-page version for wind developers, as more than 300 projects wait for review.
mission: Clearinghouse mitigation agreements

summary: President Trump signed a Section 232 proclamation concurring with Commerce that imports of wind turbines and their components threaten national security, citing radar clutter affecting defense missions, inverter cybersecurity risks and import dependence. It imposes no new tariffs but directs Commerce and USTR to negotiate with trading partners, and reserves further action if talks fail.
mission: Radar interference and cybersecurity cited in Section 232 finding
next: Commerce/USTR update on negotiations due within 180 days of the proclamation (about 2027-04-20)

summary: After national-security reviews, the Pentagon clears proposed wind projects in Maine and South Dakota, the first of about 30 of roughly 300 stalled projects the administration has reportedly promised to let proceed, a step a White House official tied to winning support for the bipartisan permitting bill.
mission: Clearinghouse review of military operations impacts
next: More authorizations expected in the coming days and weeks

summary: Commerce moves to remand the New England Wind construction and operations plan (ACK for Whales v. DOC, D.D.C.).

Plaintiffs move to enforce the August injunction, arguing DoD has not actually resumed project-specific wind reviews and that the review methodology described in its status reports keeps the freeze in place by other means; they ask the court to set specific compliance requirements (Renewable Northwest v. Hegseth, D. Or.).
mission: Clearinghouse review process

summary: Interior moves to remand its approval of the Maryland Offshore Wind plan without vacating it, citing right whale and visual impacts (Ocean City v. DOI, D. Md.).
Interior moves to remand its 2023 approval of the Revolution Wind plan for re-evaluation under OCSLA; Revolution Wind opposes (Green Oceans v. DOI, D.D.C.).
States amend their complaint over the TotalEnergies deal, adding Judgment Fund Act, Antideficiency Act and constitutional claims (New York v. DOI, D.D.C. No. 1:26-cv-01910).
project: NY Bight and Carolina Long Bay leases
mission: Settlement cites classified national security concerns; the states call the rationale pretextual

summary: Court grants BOEM summary judgment: the challenge to the December 2025 Empire Wind 1 suspension is moot because the order expired (Empire Leaseholder v. Burgum, D.D.C.).
mission: National security rationale (classified DoD report)

summary: New York and seven other states sue over the Bluepoint (E.D.N.Y.) and Invenergy (D. Me.) buyouts; California sues separately over the Invenergy Central Coast deal (N.D. Cal.).
project: NY Bight, Gulf of Maine and California leases

summary: California sues Interior over the Golden State Wind lease cancellation agreement (California v. DOI, N.D. Cal.).
mission: Interior cited unspecified national security concerns for the cancellation, per California's June notice

summary: Court grants BOEM's voluntary remand of its Atlantic Shores approval and stays the case (Save Long Beach Island v. Dep't of Commerce, D.D.C.).
RWE agrees to terminate three leases (New York Bight, California Central Coast, Gulf) for $1.22 billion, tied to natural gas investments.
next: California notice of intent to sue (2026-09-01)

summary: After an August 4 hearing, Judge Immergut grants a nationwide preliminary injunction ordering DoD to resume Clearinghouse reviews of wind projects, with status reports every 30 days (Renewable Northwest v. Hegseth, D. Or. No. 3:26-cv-01092).
mission: Clearinghouse review process
next: Merits ruling; possible Ninth Circuit appeal

summary: Fourteen senators open an inquiry into the roughly $2.7 billion in offshore wind lease buyouts, asking the companies what national-security concerns officials raised with them; answers were due August 7.
mission: Senators ask what national-security concerns were cited to leaseholders

summary: Court dismisses the OCSLA and NEPA claims in a challenge to Empire Wind; a Marine Mammal Protection Act claim remains (Save Long Beach Island v. Dep't of Commerce, D.D.C.).

A coalition of 19 attorneys general (18 states and the District of Columbia) moves to intervene in the suit over DoD's freeze on reviews of land-based wind projects, asking the court to set the freeze aside and order DoD to resume the reviews federal law requires.
mission: Clearinghouse review process

summary: Interior Secretary's Order 3451 creates a Marine Minerals Administration that absorbs BOEM, the office that leases and permits offshore wind.

Duke Energy agrees to relinquish its Carolina Long Bay lease (OCS-A 0546) for $129 million, to be reinvested in Carolinas generation and grid; the four buyback announcements to date total about $2.7 billion.

California's attorney general and Energy Commission chair send a 60-day notice of intent to sue over Interior's roughly $120 million agreement ending the Golden State Wind lease off Morro Bay, alleging OCSLA violations; the Energy Commission also subpoenas Invenergy for its settlement agreement.
mission: Notice says Interior cited unspecified national security concerns for an area already reviewed with DoD consultation

summary: Interior announces a settlement under which Invenergy affiliates terminate four leases (New York Bight, Gulf of Maine, California Central Coast) and redirect $765 million to gas plants and geothermal projects; the release calls it a partial reimbursement.
mission: Interior Secretary says the assumption that the leases raised no national security concerns proved false

summary: Sen. King adds an amendment to the Senate's FY2027 NDAA to revise the statute governing Clearinghouse review of wind projects.
mission: Clearinghouse review process
next: NDAA conference in the lame-duck session

summary: Government voluntarily dismisses its First Circuit appeal, leaving in place the ruling that vacated the day-one wind permitting pause (New York v. Trump).

Seven states (New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Vermont) sue Interior, BOEM and DOJ over the TotalEnergies lease cancellation, raising APA, NEPA, OCSLA and Judgment Fund Act claims (New York v. DOI, D.D.C. No. 1:26-cv-01910).
project: NY Bight and Carolina Long Bay leases
mission: Settlement cites classified national security concerns raised by the Department of War; the complaint calls the rationale pretextual

summary: Trade groups and environmental organizations sue DoD over its freeze on Clearinghouse reviews of wind projects (Renewable Northwest v. Hegseth, D. Or.).
mission: Clearinghouse review process
next: Ruling on the motion to enforce the injunction (filed 2026-10-20)

summary: Rep. Magaziner and 54 other House members write to Secretary Hegseth and Assistant Secretary Marks asking the basis for DoD's halt in wind project reviews, a classified briefing and a timeline for restoring the process; the letter counts nearly 200 stalled projects, at least 35 awaiting only a DoD countersignature.
mission: Clearinghouse review process

summary: DoD stops processing wind project reviews entirely, after slowing them from August 2025; plaintiffs count more than 100 onshore projects on hold.
mission: Clearinghouse review process

summary: Interior announces agreements with Bluepoint Wind (lease OCS-A 0537, up to $765 million) and Golden State Wind (lease OCS-P 0564, about $120 million): each is reimbursed after investing an equal amount in LNG or oil and gas, and both agree not to pursue new U.S. offshore wind.
project: Bluepoint Wind and Golden State Wind leases
mission: Interior Secretary says the agreements address national security concerns at both projects; none are specified

summary: Court enters a preliminary injunction against several federal policies that slowed wind and solar reviews (Renew Northeast v. DOI, D. Mass.).

Interior issues its lease cancellation decision letter to Attentive Energy (TotalEnergies), which is to receive $795 million, the amount it paid for the lease, requested from the Judgment Fund, according to the seven-state complaint.
mission: Settlement cites classified national security concerns raised by the Department of War, per the complaint

summary: Sen. Markey and Rep. Ocasio-Cortez ask Interior Secretary Burgum to halt the nearly $1 billion TotalEnergies payment, state its legal authority and funding source, and produce the evidence behind the national security claim, with answers due April 10.
project: NY Bight and Carolina Long Bay leases
mission: Asks for the evidence behind the national security rationale

summary: Interior announces the first lease buyback: TotalEnergies gives up leases OCS-A 0538 (New York Bight) and OCS-A 0545 (Carolina Long Bay) and is reimbursed up to the $928 million it paid after investing that amount in Rio Grande LNG and oil and gas; it pledges no new U.S. offshore wind.
project: NY Bight and Carolina Long Bay leases
mission: Release cites unspecified national security concerns

summary: Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind delivers its first power to the grid from the first of 176 turbines; Dominion expects to finish the project in early 2027.
A federal court in Washington dismisses most of a challenge to the approval of South Fork Wind (No. 1:23-cv-03510).

E&E News reports that Interior has begun moving solar projects on public land again while wind remains stalled: the Jackalope project was withdrawn, Maestro was canceled, and Two Rivers and Salmon Falls have not advanced.
The Justice Department lets the deadline pass without appealing the injunction that allowed Revolution Wind to resume construction.

IEEE Spectrum reports that offshore wind farms can degrade military radar and subsea sensing but that the effects have practical fixes used abroad for over a decade, citing a 2024 DOE report, a European Defence Agency study and a UK test of an air-defence radar mounted on a wind farm.
mission: Radar interference and mitigation

summary: The government appeals to the First Circuit the December ruling that vacated the pause on federal wind approvals (No. 26-01174).
Court enjoins the Sunrise Wind stop-work order; all five December suspensions are now blocked (Sunrise Wind v. Burgum, D.D.C.).
mission: National security rationale (classified DoD report)

summary: The Fish and Wildlife Service resumes eagle take permitting for wind facilities after about a year's halt, issuing 34 permits.
Courts enjoin the stop-work orders on Revolution Wind (Jan 12), Empire Wind (Jan 15), Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind (Jan 16) and Vineyard Wind 1 (Jan 27).
mission: National security rationale (classified DoD report)

summary: Reps. Kiggans, LaLota and Garbarino write to Secretaries Hegseth and Burgum asking for the analysis behind the offshore wind halt, including how it weighed radar interference and national security, and naming Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind.
mission: Asks how radar interference and national security were weighed

summary: New York and NYSERDA file two suits challenging the December stop-work orders on Sunrise Wind and Empire Wind (New York v. Burgum, D.D.C. Nos. 26-cv-00071 and 26-cv-00072).
mission: National security rationale (classified DoD report)

summary: Sens. Gillibrand and Schumer ask Interior and DoD to reverse the pause on five offshore wind leases, naming Empire Wind 1 and Sunrise Wind, and to give their offices access to the classified DoD reports cited for it by January 23.
mission: Requests the classified DoD reports behind the pause

summary: Clean energy trade groups sue Interior and other agencies in Massachusetts federal court over six policies that slow wind and solar permitting (Renew Northeast v. Department of the Interior, No. 25-cv-13961).
Sens. Markey and Warren ask Interior and DoD for access to the classified DoD reports Interior cited in pausing leases for offshore wind projects under construction, naming Vineyard Wind 1.
mission: Requests the classified DoD reports behind the pause

summary: Developers sue over Interior's December 22 national-security suspension of five offshore projects: Dominion on December 23, Empire Wind on January 2, Sunrise Wind on January 6 and Vineyard Wind on January 15.
project: Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind; Empire Wind; Sunrise Wind; Vineyard Wind
mission: Suspension cited classified national-security findings

summary: Interior pauses the leases of all five projects under construction for 90 days, citing national security risks in a classified DoD report, including radar clutter.
mission: Radar interference; classified DoD report

summary: Court grants the states summary judgment, holding unlawful and vacating the agencies' implementation of the January 2025 pause on wind authorizations (New York v. Trump, D. Mass. No. 1:25-cv-11221).
Court denies BOEM's motion for voluntary remand of the Maryland Offshore Wind approval, which BOEM said rested on an error it had identified (Ocean City v. DOI, D. Md. No. 1:24-cv-03111).
Court grants BOEM's motion for voluntary remand of the SouthCoast Wind approval so the agency can reconsider it, and stays the case (Town and County of Nantucket v. Burgum, D.D.C. No. 1:25-cv-00906).
Court grants a preliminary injunction blocking the August stop-work order on Revolution Wind (Revolution Wind v. Burgum, D.D.C. No. 1:25-cv-02999).
Army Corps of Engineers guidance directs districts to prioritize permit applications for projects that produce more energy per acre, which puts wind behind other sources.
The Transportation Department withdraws or cancels $679 million in grants for 12 port projects tied to offshore wind.
BOEM orders Revolution Wind to stop work on the nearly complete project; the developer and the states of Rhode Island and Connecticut sue on September 4.
mission: Stop-work order cited national security concerns

summary: In court filings between August 22 and September 3, Interior says it will reconsider its approvals of the Maryland Offshore Wind, SouthCoast Wind and New England Wind projects.
project: Maryland Offshore Wind; SouthCoast Wind; New England Wind
next: Remand motions decided project by project

summary: IRS Notice 2025-42 narrows how wind and solar projects can show they began construction in time to claim tax credits, ending the 5 percent spending safe harbor for most projects.
Commerce opens a Section 232 national-security investigation into imports of wind turbines and their parts.
mission: Investigation asks whether turbine imports threaten national security

summary: Interior cancels the approval of the Lava Ridge wind project on federal land in Idaho, which BLM had approved in December 2024.

BOEM publishes a direct final rule rescinding 30 CFR 585.150, the requirement to publish a five-year schedule of renewable lease sales, effective September 4; the preamble says the January 2025 withdrawal under OCSLA section 12(a) blocks future renewable leasing while it stays in effect (90 FR 37386).
An Interior memo directs the Fish and Wildlife Service to review wind projects' compliance with the Bald and Golden Eagle Protection Act and the eagle permit program.
Interior Secretary's Order 3438 directs the department to weigh a project's capacity density (energy produced per acre) when permitting on federal land, a test that disfavors wind and solar.
BOEM rescinds all designated Wind Energy Areas, about 3.5 million acres; areas already leased are not affected.

Interior Secretary's Order 3437 ends what it calls preferential treatment for wind and directs reviews of wind's effects, including a report on the consequences of wind development for bird mortality and for military readiness.
mission: Order asks for reports on wind's effect on military readiness

summary: The Transportation Department announces it will review wind turbines sited near highways and railroads and recommends a larger setback from them.
An Interior memo requires review by the Secretary's office of 69 types of wind and solar actions, from rights-of-way to consultations, before they can proceed.

Executive Order 14315 directs Treasury to tighten the rules on when a wind or solar project counts as having begun construction for tax-credit purposes, and directs Interior to review policies that favor wind and solar.
EPA tells Maryland that the state air permit for US Wind's Maryland Offshore Wind project was issued with the wrong appeal process and must be reissued.

The budget reconciliation law signed July 4 ends the clean electricity tax credits early for wind and solar, setting construction-start and in-service deadlines that new projects must meet to qualify.
Atlantic Shores asks New Jersey regulators to cancel its state power contract, citing the loss of its air permit and federal policy; the state grants the request on August 13.
actor: New Jersey Board of Public Utilities

summary: Interior lifts the April stop-work order on Empire Wind 1, and construction resumes.
A coalition of states sues in Massachusetts federal court over the January 2025 presidential wind memorandum and the halt on federal wind approvals (New York v. Trump, No. 1:25-cv-11221).

Interior's Solicitor withdraws the Biden-era legal opinion on how offshore wind approvals weigh other ocean uses and reinstates the first-term opinion, which makes it easier to deny or reconsider a project over interference with other uses.
The Interior Secretary directs BOEM to order Empire Wind to stop work; BOEM later reverses the order, and opponents sue over the reversal on June 3.

GAO publishes its review of Interior's offshore wind oversight (GAO-25-106998, released April 14), listing defense and radar systems among the areas turbines could affect and noting that the extent of some impacts is not yet known.
mission: Radar interference

summary: EPA's appeals board sends the Atlantic Shores air permit back to the agency at EPA's request, leaving the project without a valid air permit.
next: Developer sought to cancel its New Jersey contract 2025-06-04

summary: A presidential memorandum withdraws the entire Outer Continental Shelf from wind leasing under OCSLA section 12(a) until revoked, and directs agencies to issue no new or renewed approvals for onshore or offshore wind pending a review; existing leases are left in place but put under review (90 FR 8363).
The Supreme Court declines to hear a challenge to the federal approval of Vineyard Wind (No. 23-337), leaving the First Circuit ruling for the government in place.
Interior approves SouthCoast Wind, a project of up to 2.4 GW off Massachusetts and the eleventh commercial-scale offshore wind project approved.
BOEM holds the first commercial lease sale in the Gulf of Maine; four of the eight lease areas offered are sold.

BOEM and DoD sign a memorandum of understanding on offshore wind: collaborate early in leasing, share information, and determine which areas should be deferred from leasing for military activities. It builds on the 1983 DoD-Interior agreement on the Outer Continental Shelf.
mission: DoD-BOEM coordination on military mission compatibility
